newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Comedian Cosby to lighten up S. Africa jail island.
newsitem.headline: Comedian Cosby to lighten up S. Africa jail island.

text.p: U.S. comedian Bill Cosby cracked jokes with President Nelson Mandela on Thursday and vowed to bring "fun and laughter" to South Africa's vale of tears, Robben Island.
Cosby is the star of a fund-raising dinner on the island, a former jail and now a museum of the apartheid era, on Thursday night. About 70 guests are paying 125,000 rand ($28,000) a head.
"This is all fun and laughter this time," Cosby told reporters after meeting Mandela at his official Cape Town residence. "There's no solemness, we are celebrating."
In an unintended piece of slapstick comedy, a bus due to have been used by celebrities on the island plunged into the sea when a cable suspending it from a helicopter snapped.
Mandela spent 18 years on Robben Island as part of a life sentence imposed by the apartheid government for his attempts to overthrow it by force.
Proceeds from the dinner will go to help the families of former political prisoners and to develop the museum on the island.
Among the guests will be Hillary Rodham Clinton, wife of the U.S. president, and U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
